title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Decision on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Decision on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation

Fa Fa [2021] No. 20

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all units of this Court:

The Decision on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation was adopted at the 1841st session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 8, 2021, and is hereby issued to you for compliance and implementation.

June 9, 2021

Decision on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation

(Adopted at the 1841st session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 8, 2021, effective from June 16, 2021)

Based on the needs of trial and enforcement work, it is decided at the 1841st session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court to amend the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation as follows:

The first paragraph of Article 6 is amended to read: "The forms of judicial interpretation are divided into five types: 'Interpretation', 'Provisions', 'Rules', 'Reply', and 'Decision'."

A new paragraph is added after the third paragraph of Article 6 as the fourth paragraph: "For judicial interpretations that regulate the trial and enforcement activities of people's courts, the form of 'Rules' may be adopted."

The original fourth and fifth paragraphs of Article 6 become the fifth and sixth paragraphs of Article 6.

This Decision shall come into effect on June 16, 2021.

In accordance with this Decision, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation shall be revised accordingly and re-promulgated.

Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation

(Adopted at the 1408th session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 11, 2006, effective from April 1, 2007. Revised in accordance with the Decision on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation adopted at the 1841st session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 8, 2021; such Decision shall come into effect on June 16, 2021)

I. General Provisions

Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the Supervision Law of the Standing Committees of the People's Congresses at All Levels of the People's Republic of China, the Resolution of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Strengthening the Work of Legal Interpretation, and other relevant provisions, for the purpose of further regulating and improving the work of judicial interpretation.

Article 2 Issues concerning the specific application of law by people's courts in trial work shall be subject to judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 3 Judicial interpretations shall be formulated in accordance with the law and relevant legislative intent, taking into account the actual needs of trial work.

Article 4 Judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court shall be discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee.

Article 5 Judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court have legal effect.

Article 6 The forms of judicial interpretation are divided into five types: "Interpretation", "Provisions", "Rules", "Reply", and "Decision".

Judicial interpretations formulated on how to specifically apply a certain law in trial work, or how to apply law to a certain category of cases or a certain type of issue, shall adopt the form of "Interpretation".

Judicial interpretations, such as norms and opinions, that need to be formulated in trial work based on legislative intent shall adopt the form of "Provisions".

For judicial interpretations that regulate the trial and enforcement activities of people's courts, the form of "Rules" may be adopted.

Judicial interpretations formulated in response to requests from High People's Courts and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army on issues concerning the specific application of law in trial work shall adopt the form of "Reply".

Judicial interpretations amending or abolishing other judicial interpretations shall adopt the form of "Decision".

Article 7 The work of jointly formulating judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall be handled in accordance with legal provisions and the consensus reached by both parties through consultation.

Article 8 The Research Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be uniformly responsible for the project initiation, review, coordination, and other work of judicial interpretations.

II. Project Initiation

Article 9 The formulation of a judicial interpretation shall be subject to project initiation.

Article 10 The sources of project initiation for the formulation of judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court are:

(1) Requests by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court to formulate a judicial interpretation;

(2) Proposals by the trial departments of the Supreme People's Court to formulate a judicial interpretation;

(3) Proposals by High People's Courts and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army to formulate a judicial interpretation, or requests for instruction on issues of law application;

(4) Motions or proposals by deputies to the National People's Congress or members of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference to formulate a judicial interpretation;

(5) Proposals by relevant state organs, social organizations, or other organizations, as well as citizens, to formulate a judicial interpretation;

(6) Other circumstances under which the Supreme People's Court deems it necessary to formulate a judicial interpretation.

If Primary People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts consider it necessary to formulate a judicial interpretation, they shall report it level by level to the High People's Court, which shall review and decide whether to submit a proposal for formulating a judicial interpretation or a request for instruction on issues of law application to the Supreme People's Court.

Article 11 If the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court requests the formulation of a judicial interpretation, the Research Office shall directly initiate the project.

For other sources of project initiation for formulating a judicial interpretation, the Research Office shall review whether to initiate the project.

Article 12 If the trial departments of the Supreme People's Court intend to formulate judicial interpretations of the "Interpretation" or "Provisions" type, they shall submit a project initiation proposal for the following year to the Research Office by the end of each year.

The Research Office shall consolidate the project initiation proposals, draft an annual project initiation plan for judicial interpretations, and after approval by the court leader in charge, submit it to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision.

Under special circumstances, if it is necessary to add or adjust a project initiation for a judicial interpretation, the relevant department shall submit a proposal, and the Research Office shall, after reporting to the court leader in charge for approval, report to the Executive Vice President or the President for decision.

Article 13 If the trial departments of the Supreme People's Court intend to formulate a "Reply" in response to a request from a High People's Court or the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, they shall promptly submit a project initiation proposal to the Research Office for review and project initiation.

Article 14 The project initiation plan for judicial interpretations shall include the following content: source of project initiation, necessity of the project initiation, main issues requiring interpretation, drafting plan for the judicial interpretation, responsible department, and other necessary matters.

Article 15 Judicial interpretations shall be completed in accordance with the project initiation plan discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee. If a judicial interpretation cannot be completed in accordance with the project initiation plan, the drafting department shall promptly submit a written explanation. The Research Office shall, after reporting to the court leader in charge for approval, submit it to the Judicial Committee to decide whether to continue the project initiation.

III. Drafting and Submission

Article 16 The drafting of judicial interpretations shall be the responsibility of the trial departments of the Supreme People's Court.

For comprehensive judicial interpretations involving the functional scope of different trial departments, the Research Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for drafting or organizing and coordinating the relevant departments to draft.

Article 17 When drafting a judicial interpretation, in-depth investigation and research shall be conducted, trial practice experience shall be earnestly summarized, and opinions shall be widely solicited.

For judicial interpretations involving the vital interests of the people or major difficult issues, after approval by the court leader in charge and reporting to the Executive Vice President or the President for decision, opinions may be publicly solicited from society.

Article 18 The draft for review of a judicial interpretation shall be submitted to the relevant special committee of the National People's Congress or the relevant working department of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for comments.

Article 19 Before submitting the draft for review of a judicial interpretation to the Judicial Committee for discussion, the drafting department shall submit the draft for review and its explanatory notes to the Research Office for review.

The draft for review of a judicial interpretation and its explanatory notes shall include: the project initiation plan, investigation and research report, summary of opinions solicited, review opinion of the Vice President in charge on whether to submit for review, main contentious issues, and relevant laws, regulations, judicial interpretations, and other relevant materials.

Article 20 The Research Office shall mainly review the following content:

(1) Whether it conforms to the provisions of the Constitution and laws;

(2) Whether it exceeds the scope of authority for judicial interpretation;

(3) Whether it duplicates or conflicts with relevant judicial interpretations;

(4) Whether it has been carried out in accordance with the prescribed procedures;

(5) Whether the submitted materials meet the requirements;

(6) Whether the main opinions of relevant parties are fully and objectively reflected;

(7) Whether the main contentious issues and solutions are clear;

(8) Other content that should be reviewed.

The Research Office shall issue a review opinion within one month.

Article 21 If the Research Office considers that the draft for review of a judicial interpretation requires further revision, argumentation, or coordination, it shall work together with the drafting department to carry out revision, argumentation, or coordination.

Article 22 After the Research Office reviews the draft for review of a judicial interpretation and forms a draft, the drafting department shall submit it to the court leader in charge and the Executive Vice President for approval before referring it to the Judicial Committee for discussion.

IV. Discussion

Article 23 The Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court shall discuss the draft of a judicial interpretation within three months from the day after its submission. If it fails to discuss it within the time limit, the Office of the Judicial Committee may, with the approval of the Executive Vice President, extend the time limit.

Article 24 If the draft of a judicial interpretation is discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee, it shall be signed and issued by the President or the Executive Vice President.

If the draft of a judicial interpretation is discussed and adopted in principle by the Judicial Committee, the drafting department, together with the Research Office, shall make revisions in accordance with the decision of the Judicial Committee discussion, and after reporting to the Vice President in charge for review, it shall be signed and issued by the President or the Executive Vice President.

If the Judicial Committee considers that the conditions for formulating a judicial interpretation are not yet mature, it may decide to further argue, postpone discussion, or revoke the project initiation.

V. Publication, Implementation, and Recordation

Article 25 Judicial interpretations shall be published in the form of an Announcement of the Supreme People's Court.

Judicial interpretations shall be published in the Gazette of the Supreme People's Court and the People's Court Daily.

Judicial interpretations shall take effect from the date of publication of the Announcement, unless otherwise provided in the judicial interpretation.

Article 26 Judicial interpretations shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for recordation within thirty days from the date of publication.

The submission for recordation shall be the responsibility of the General Office, and other related work shall be the responsibility of the Research Office.

Article 27 After a judicial interpretation takes effect, if a people's court uses it as a basis for adjudication, it shall be cited in judicial documents.

If a people's court cites both laws and judicial interpretations as the basis for adjudication, the laws shall be cited first, followed by the judicial interpretation.

Article 28 The Supreme People's Court shall supervise the application of judicial interpretations by local people's courts at all levels and special people's courts in trial work. Higher people's courts shall supervise the application of judicial interpretations by lower people's courts in trial work.

VI. Compilation, Amendment, and Abolition

Article 29 The compilation of judicial interpretations shall be decided by the Judicial Committee, and the specific work shall be the responsibility of the Research Office, with the participation of all trial departments.

Article 30 If a judicial interpretation needs to be amended or abolished, the relevant provisions on the procedure for formulating judicial interpretations shall be referred to, and the matter shall be discussed and decided by the Judicial Committee.

Article 31 These Provisions shall come into effect on April 1, 2007. The Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation, issued on July 1, 1997, shall be simultaneously abolished.
